deck.free: Only the initial ten normal bases; acquired copies each authorize one starting instance. A historical unlock alone does not authorize a free acquired card.
deck.variant_selection: One copy per reward base in the listed order; then replace one initial normal card per base with an owned affixed copy. Prefer fewer affixes, canonical key, then possession ID. This deliberately simple rule does not claim optimal builds.

journey.passives: AR adapt with cost capacity 8; unchanged learning priority and sale policy
journey.purchase: Reserve the cost of unlearned bases; among affordable AT candidates prefer a card, otherwise a learned passive, then candidate ID. One purchase per batch at the unchanged AT price. No future draw or reward lookup.

paired.seed: Next seed in each checkpoint's existing sequence, identical across deck/policy/route alternatives

measurements: Natural returns, purchase, owned card selection, learning and changing available routes
Paired clear/defeat and clear-only player actions, separated by route, stage and policy
Before/after the player's first refill from the shared discard pool; this is NOT the start of all mixing, because other actors can refill earlier
Owned initial cards used by P, used by NPCs, or consumed as field material; borrowed card use
Distinct target choice opportunities, progress/side policy disagreement and consecutive same target/mode actions within an unchanged event
Actual traversal boundaries, reward protection and immediate-withdrawal alternatives at those boundaries
limits: Conditions fixed before the AU comparison; natural 32 runs plus at most 96 paired forks. No favorable seed selection, runtime-stat adjustment, exhaustive optimization, new scenario content or actual human test.
Free deck selection and acquired-copy selection are preparation APIs, not an implemented preparation UI. The old browser prototypes remain unchanged.
The count-based AH runtime is adapted at launch; persistent AP possession IDs remain separate from exploration card IDs. No saleable copy is minted by launch, refill, use or return.
The two deck alternatives share one checkpoint, learning/equipment and combat seed. Subsequent rewards in paired forks are not accumulated into the natural history.
Repeated target/mode is only a review cue. Public values, hand, field and timing can still change. Mechanical counts do not establish boredom, comprehension or fun.
Progression stages are a design proposal. Basic design 0.53 and D53 remain unchanged; no formal capacity, price, card-count or campaign-end adoption.
